title: SNL Stories from the Show- Unreleased (Eddie Murphy, John Mulaney and More)
text: Josh Brolin, when he hosted, Sarah Palin came on, which was the same night that Will Forte first submitted Fartface. His given name is Carl, and he likes to be called Fartface. So at Dress, the sketch does terribly. Fartface! But it gets in. Everyone has a sense everyone in America is watching. And then Josh Brolin, he's looking up here at the bleaches like this. And he's just nodding at them. And he looks at Forte and Bill, and he goes, let's shut these f***s up. And that was the Emmy episode. They're not really pranks. We did a lot of stuff waiting for Lauren at the read-through. Because, you know, you're always waiting a little bit, and so we sang happy birthday for him when it was just not his birthday. He was like, oh, good, thank you. But he kind of was smiling. I think he, yeah. There wasn't a screen test. There was a series of auditions. The first time I came here was, uh, just Neil Levy, just me and Neil in his office. And he said, uh, make me laugh. And he sat back and I did my shtick. And luckily, because I was doing stand-up already. See, I think a lot of actors come, somebody say, make me laugh, and you don't have an act. It might be pretty daunting. I did Ali, Muhammad Ali and Howard Cosell and Jimmy Carter. That's how long ago it was. Jimmy Carter impression. And I did, uh, Bill Cosby. And he didn't laugh at all. And he just sat and kind of looked at me. And he just said, thank you. And then I laughed. I was like, well, I guess I didn't get it. Then a couple weeks later, they called me and said, come in. We want to see you again. Then I went back. This time it was, uh, two people in a room and they said, make me laugh again. And I did the same thing again. And they said, thank you. Then another week or two went by and they called me back again. And then I went and it was Liz Welch, Neil Levy, and Mike Zanella. And he was the producer, one of the producers on the show. And he said, uh, make us laugh. And I did all my stuff. And, uh, and Mike Zanella was in the back and he, he did like this. That was my big laugh. That was the big laugh of the three auditions. We did a sketch, um, called Blockbuster where I played like a hobo woman. And we literally shot all day and all night until about 7 30 in the morning. And then had to be back here at noon. So the turnaround was horrible. And I basically like slept here as if it was my home. And. Then washed like my hands and feet in the sink. I mostly use this space to like recoup in some way. I think when people think of SNL, they think of people doing Coke and mostly it's me sitting right here with a blanket on.
